purpose: Score SocratiCode against a scoped rg keyword baseline on the same sealed 35-question set (recall, MRR) with a decoy second-project index, to give the 'comparative recall ... cross-project isolation' gap a first measured comparison instead of no comparison at all.
preregistered: Point SocratiCode's own MCP server at the disposable Qdrant instance via QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_MODE=external env vars (never the live 127.0.0.1:16333), with a distinct QDRANT_COLLECTION_PREFIX and a redirected SOCRATICODE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR, keeping LMSTUDIO_URL pointed at the permitted read-only live embedding endpoint. If SocratiCode cannot be pointed at the disposable Qdrant without touching live config, record it as not run and score only rg (and QMD if applicable) on the sealed set. If it can: run codebase_index to completion (poll codebase_status until the index is no longer 'in progress'), then codebase_search for all 35 sealed questions, score Recall@5/MRR with the same line-overlap rule as the embedder-arm benchmark, and additionally index a small decoy second project into the same disposable Qdrant instance and confirm a decoy-project search for agent-lab-specific terms never returns an agent-lab path (cross-project leakage = 0 is the pass condition). QMD (Markdown-only per this project's own scope note) is not expected to score meaningfully on this code-only gold-span set and is recorded as not applicable rather than run as a token gesture.

result: On this sealed 35-question set: SocratiCode Recall@5=0.857 (30/35), MRR=0.721 (from the completed-index run; an earlier, now-disclosed run against a 52%-complete index scored 0.486/0.379 and was superseded, not silently dropped -- see commands above and CORRECTED notes below). Scoped rg-keyword baseline Recall@5=0.571 (20/35), MRR=0.289. CORRECTED (fix round): the original claim that 'SocratiCode meaningfully outperforms the literal rg baseline' overstates what this specific comparison establishes. rg_baseline.py ranks its top-5 by rg's own file-traversal order (no --sort, no relevance ranking) over the first 5 hits of at most 6 keyword queries, not by any notion of definition-site or relevance; a large majority of the 35 sealed questions additionally name the exact identifier defined at (or near) the gold span (see held-out-recall-benchmark.json's corrected limitations for the count check), which a keyword search should trivially find if the ranking heuristic surfaced the right file first. The measured gap (0.857/0.721 vs 0.571/0.289) is real and reproducible from the retained raw artifacts, but is at least partly attributable to this baseline's weak ranking heuristic rather than solely to a fundamental limit of scoped literal search -- so it should be read as 'SocratiCode beat this specific, not-relevance-ranked rg heuristic', not as an established general claim that SocratiCode outperforms scoped literal search per se. Cross-project isolation held in the one decoy trial run (0 leaked hits out of 1 decoy-project result; each project gets its own Qdrant collection by construction). QMD was assessed as not applicable to this code-only gold-span set, not run as a baseline. SocratiCode's own Recall@5/MRR (0.857/0.721) sit between the rg baseline (0.571/0.289) and the raw incumbent-embedder-direct benchmark (0.971/0.853 for the same questions against the same corpus with 2x the chunk density, no reranking-vs-raw-vector difference, and no code-graph overhead) -- the gap between SocratiCode and the raw-embedding arm A is plausibly attributable to SocratiCode's own chunking/graph/reranking pipeline differing from this benchmark's fixed 20-line chunker, not to a worse embedding model (it uses the same Nemotron-3-Embed-1B endpoint); this attribution is not independently verified here.

verdict_impact.explanation: CORRECTED (fix round): downgraded from 'supports_incumbent' to 'inconclusive' for the comparative-recall claim specifically. Gives gap 7 its first measured recall/MRR/leakage numbers instead of none, and the one decoy-isolation trial genuinely supports zero cross-project leakage by construction (that narrow finding stays supported). But the comparative 'SocratiCode > rg' recall/MRR direction rests on a literal-match baseline (rg_baseline.py) that ranks hits by unordered file-traversal position rather than relevance, against a question set where most questions name the gold span's own defined identifier -- so a stronger, relevance- or definition-aware literal baseline could plausibly close some or all of the measured gap, and this check alone does not establish that SocratiCode outperforms scoped literal search in general. It does NOT settle 'grounded answer accuracy ... latency or resource superiority' against a broader baseline set (QMD was not applicable here; only one decoy-isolation trial was run, not a stress test).

limitations: One decoy-project trial only, not an adversarial or larger-scale leakage stress test.
QMD was not run (assessed as not applicable to a code-only gold-span set); the gap's 'rg/QMD baselines' language is only half-covered by measured evidence.

CORRECTED (fix round): rg baseline uses a simple keyword-extraction heuristic (longest non-stopword identifiers) AND ranks its top-5 by unordered rg file-traversal position, not by relevance or definition-site proximity, and has no --sort flag so its own ordering is not guaranteed stable; combined with most sealed questions naming the gold span's own defined identifier, this makes it a weak (strawman) baseline for a 'SocratiCode outperforms literal search' claim specifically, though the raw recall/MRR numbers themselves are accurately reported and reproducible.

SocratiCode's pipeline (chunking, code graph, hybrid ranking) differs from this benchmark's own fixed chunker, so this receipt cannot isolate whether SocratiCode's edge over rg comes from its embedding model, its chunking, or its graph/reranking.
Grounded-answer-accuracy and latency/resource-superiority claims named in the gap text were not scored in this check.
